summary: Ansible can be installed in a virtualenv on the control node with pip; libraries not on pip such as SELinux bindings need --system-site-packages or must be copied into the virtualenv manually.
questions: How do I install Ansible in a virtualenv?
SELinux bindings aren't available in my Ansible venv, how do I fix it?

answer_card.title: Install Ansible in a virtualenv
answer_card.answer_md:
```bash
virtualenv -p python3 ansible
source ./ansible/bin/activate
pip install ansible
```

For libraries pip can't provide (e.g. **SELinux bindings** on RHEL/Fedora), either create the venv with `--system-site-packages`, or copy them in, e.g. `/usr/lib64/python3.*/site-packages/selinux/` and `*selinux*.so` into the venv's `site-packages`.
